endorsements.quote: All AI-generated questions should be grounded in specific course material rather than the AI's general knowledge.
We strongly recommend that all AI-generated questions undergo expert human review before distribution.
We suggest a phased approach for the introduction of AI-generated MCQs, beginning with low-stakes or formative assessments before progressing to higher-stakes examinations.
Faculty should be trained to identify and mitigate such potential issues.
Students should be informed that assessments contain questions written by AI, even if only in part.
To this end, faculty should maintain oversight responsibilities of all assessments regardless of whether questions are AI-generated or traditionally authored.

Prompt engineering skills — the ability to effectively instruct AI systems to produce desired outputs — cannot be assumed and may necessitate the development of web portals that scaffold the question generation process.

unlisted_practices: Introduce feedback mechanisms so students can raise concerns about particular AI-generated questions or assessments.
Institutions should develop and distribute guidelines and checklists for reviewing AI-generated questions.
Use multiple levels of review, including senior faculty with relevant expertise, for high-stakes AI-generated assessments.
Integrate AI question generation systems with existing learning management systems to limit student data privacy exposure.
Institutions should develop student-facing policies on faculty AI use, including disclosure requirements and justification for differences from student restrictions.
Keep faculty adoption of AI question generation optional rather than mandated.
Institutions should document AI usage across the assessment creation lifecycle, including prompts, human modifications, and quality assurance decisions, preferably collected automatically.
Map each AI-generated question to specific learning outcomes and Bloom's Taxonomy levels and document the mapping.
Use automated quality checks to screen AI-generated questions for bias, ambiguity, incorrect answer keys, and overlap before human review.
Continually reevaluate the use of AI in assessment as validation data accumulates and models advance.

screen.reason: This is a commentary/perspective providing practical guiding principles and implementation considerations for using AI-generated multiple-choice questions in health science education.
